title: TST: add regression test for read_sql with % in text and selectables (GH#35484)

labels.name: Needs Issue Assignment
labels.description: PR whose author is not assigned to a linked issue

body:
Adds a regression test to pandas/tests/io/test_sql.py that verifies queries containing a literal % work correctly when passed via sqlalchemy.text() or sqlalchemy.select(), returning 1 for 5 % 2. This addresses GH#35484 by ensuring future refactors don’t silently break escaped‑percent handling in SQLAlchemy selectables. The plain‑string case is excluded because it still fails on MySQL and PostgreSQL due to driver interpolation rules, and that behavior is already covered by the existing test_read_sql_iris_no_parameter_with_percent (marked xfail). Locally the new test passed on SQLite and PostgreSQL with psycopg2, while MySQL was left to CI. title: BUG: GroupBy.agg with as_index=False and MultiIndex column grouping key raises ValueError

labels.name: Needs Issue Assignment
labels.description: PR whose author is not assigned to a linked issue

body:
---
Closes GH-39103

---

### Reproduction

```python
df = pd.DataFrame({("col0", "l0"): [0, 0, 1], ("col1", "l1"): [10, 20, 30]})
df.groupby(("col0", "l0"), as_index=False).agg({("col1", "l1"): ["min", "max"]})
```

```text
ValueError: Item must have length equal to number of levels.
```

### Root cause

`_insert_inaxis_grouper` in `pandas/core/groupby/groupby.py` decides whether the `as_index=False` group key has already been inserted by the aggregation itself. For a `MultiIndex` columns frame, the str-name path pads the key to the columns' `nlevels` (`("key", "", ...)`, per GH-17024 / GH-28549), but a tuple name of fewer levels than `result.columns.nlevels` was returned unchanged, and `result.insert(0, name, lev)` then failed with the "Item must have length equal to number of levels" `ValueError`.

### Fix

`full_key()` now also pads tuple names when `len(name) < result.columns.nlevels`, and the membership check uses `full_key(name)` so it looks up the exact key that will be inserted (previously a partial-tuple lookup which additionally raised `PerformanceWarning` on un-lex-sorted `MultiIndex` columns, surfaced as an error under CI's `filterwarnings`).

The inserted grouper column now exactly matches the canonical `groupby(..., as_index=True).agg(...).reset_index()` output.

### Verification

- Issue repro now returns the expected padded columns `[("col0", "l0", ""), ("col1", "l1", "min"), ("col1", "l1", "max")]`, byte-identical to the `as_index=True` + `reset_index()` form for `agg`, `describe`, and multi-tuple-grouper cases
- New tests: `test_groupby_agg_as_index_false_multiindex_column` (padded columns, existing column order, empty input) and `test_groupby_as_index_false_multiindex_column_matches_reset_index` (agg/describe/multi-tuple equivalence)
- `pandas/tests/groupby/`: 24447 passed, 866 skipped, 43 xfailed
- Sweep of `pandas/tests/resample/`, `pandas/tests/apply/`, `pandas/tests/reshape/`: green (2 unrelated pre-existing tzdata DST failures, confirmed identical on `main`)
- `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean (repo-pinned ruff 0.16.6); `aggregate/` suite green under `-W error`

title: DOC: Fix read_hdf example to pass key as keyword argument (#69255)
body:
## What

The `read_hdf` docstring example calls `df.to_hdf("./store.h5", "data")`, but the second argument (`key`) is keyword-only in the public signature. This PR updates the example to the correct keyword form:

```python
df.to_hdf("./store.h5", key="data")
```

## Why

Copying the current example raises `TypeError: to_hdf() takes 1 positional argument but 2 were given` (or similar positional-argument error), so the documented example does not run as written.

## Changes

- `pandas/io/pytables.py`: one-line docstring fix in the `read_hdf` Examples section.

title: BUG: account for engine-retained object values in Index.memory_usage(deep=True) for arrow-backed indexes

labels.name: Needs Issue Assignment
labels.description: PR whose author is not assigned to a linked issue

body:
- [x] closes #66593
- [x] [Tests added and passed](https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/dev/development/contributing_codebase.html#writing-tests) if fixing a bug or adding a new feature

Check exactly one of the following, per the [automated contributions policy](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/dev/development/contributing.html#automated-contributions-policy):
- [ ] I did **not** use AI to develop this pull request.
- [x] I used AI to develop this pull request. I prompted it to follow `AGENTS.md`, I have reviewed and understood every change, and I have described above how I used it and exactly which tool, model version, and effort setting — e.g. `claude opus 4.8 (xhigh)`, not just `claude`.

## What happened

As reported in #66593: for an arrow-backed string `Index`, `_get_engine_target()` returns `vals.astype(object)` — a distinct object-dtype copy that the cached lookup engine retains for its lifetime — and `memory_usage(deep=True)` accounted for neither that array nor its `PyUnicode` payloads. On the reporter's 500k-row repro only the hashtable growth (~16.9 MB) was reported where ~61 MB was actually allocated (3.6x under-report).

## What I did

`Index.memory_usage` now adds, when `deep=True` and the engine's mapping is populated:

- `engine.values.nbytes` — the retained pointer array, and
- `lib.memory_usage_of_objects(engine.values)` — its boxed strings,

**only** when the engine's array is an object-dtype copy that was not already counted, i.e. the Index's own array is an `ArrowExtensionArray` and the engine's array is neither `self._values` nor `self._values._ndarray`. This keeps the shared-array cases exactly as before:

- `object` dtype: engine array *is* `self._values` → unchanged
- `string[python]`: engine array *is* `StringArray._ndarray` → unchanged
- arrow-backed `str`/`string`: engine owns an exclusive copy → now counted

This is the shape the issue itself suggested (count the engine's retained values plus `lib.memory_usage_of_objects` when deep and not shared). Accounting was placed in `Index.memory_usage` rather than in `IndexEngine.sizeof`/`HashTable.sizeof` because the engine cannot tell whether its array is shared with the Index — only the Index knows that — so doing it in the engine risks double-counting the `object`/`string[python]` cases.

Note on exactness: as in the existing deep accounting for object dtype, this uses `sys.getsizeof` sums (`memory_usage_of_objects`), so the number is an accounting estimate, not RSS. On the repro it now lands at 61,408 kB growth vs the ~61.4 MB the reporter measured.

### Repro numbers (Linux x86_64, built from this branch)

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| reported growth (500k × 40-byte str, `str` dtype / arrow storage) | 16,908 kB | **61,408 kB** |
| engine object array | 4,000 kB (unaccounted) | counted |
| its PyUnicodes | 40,500 kB (unaccounted) | counted |
| object-dtype growth (must not change) | 16,908 kB | 16,908 kB |
| `string[python]` growth (shares `_ndarray`; must not change) | 16,908 kB | 16,908 kB |

The propagation to `DataFrame.memory_usage(deep=True)` (one `.loc` on a string-indexed frame) is fixed transitively since it sums `Index.memory_usage(deep=True)`.

## Tests

- `tests/indexes/test_old_base.py`: two new regression tests — the arrow-backed case asserts the engine-build growth covers `held.nbytes + Σ sys.getsizeof`; the object-dtype case pins the no-double-count invariant (`after - before == engine.sizeof(deep=True)`). The first fails on main, passes here.
- `tests/base/test_misc.py::test_memory_usage`: the shared module-level fixture objects can carry a *populated* nested engine (categorical categories / MultiIndex levels) left over from earlier tests; since deep now correctly counts those engines' retained copies, the fixture setup clears nested engines recursively so each parametrization starts pristine. (Without this, `res == res_deep` fails for `categorical`/`tuples`/`multi` purely due to test-order cross-contamination, not the fix.)
- Ran: `pandas/tests/indexes` (17,906 passed; the single `tzlocal` failure reproduces on unmodified main in this environment), `pandas/tests/base` (all pass), plus `frame/methods/test_info.py`, `series/methods/test_info.py`, `arrays/categorical/test_analytics.py`, `arrays/string_/test_string.py`, `extension/base`, `apply/test_frame_apply.py`, `frame/test_subclass.py`, `arrays/sparse/test_array.py` — all pass. `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean on the touched files.

Developed with AI assistance: Hermes Agent (Nous Research), model `qwen3.8-flash`, running an interactive session against the repo per `AGENTS.md` (default effort). The AI reproduced the issue on a locally built editable install before and after the change, ran the test suites listed above, and drafted this description; every diff hunk was reviewed line-by-line.

title: TST: sparse boolean-mask getitem tests assumed op results store fill values (GH#45284)

labels.name: Sparse

body:
Three tests fail on main. The tests added in GH-69132 built their boolean mask from a comparison or logical op and asserted, as a precondition, that the result stores a value equal to its own `fill_value`. GH-69131 then made the ops prune exactly those values, so the precondition no longer holds. Each PR was green on its own base.

`SparseArray.__getitem__` still needs the GH-69132 fix: a mask given an explicit `sparse_index` can store a value equal to its fill, and both the `fill_value=False` and `fill_value=True` branches return the wrong result without it. So the mask is now built that way instead of via an op. The op-side pruning is already covered by the tests added in GH-69131.
